angle: the machine's own rule as a physical thing: what turning each knob would do to a real object
subject: The colony walking a glockenspiel, one bar per degree, so the loop the ants keep treading across the bars is the phrase they play.
controls: ants: count, contour ants walking the bright loop over the bars, 1 to 8, spaced evenly round it; each new one eases in at the lowest bar.

scent: shape, the loop itself: at 0 it frays into a loose scribble that wanders over many bars, at 100 it pulls into one tight oval over the few bars the phrase uses (outer points move well over 16 px).
fade: count, the dashed old routes still lying across the bars: two at 0 and default, none by 100, each one thinning out from its far end as it goes.
scale: count + position, the bars themselves: 11 at pent (two octaves) up to 25 at chrom, bars narrowing and sliding closer so the instrument keeps its width, the rails following.
reference: library/theseus-tower (an instrument drawn as itself, line on black)
muted: Muted: the loop drops from the bright weight to the rail grey and the ants stop where they are; the bars stay, so the instrument reads as resting.
risks: A glockenspiel is a picture of any melodic machine; only the ants and the loop make it this one, so it lives or dies on the ants reading at 26 px. The loop is a smooth oval, so which bars actually sound (landings, not crossings) isn't drawn; a note flash on the struck bar has to carry that. At chrom 25 bars are ~12 px wide with 6 px gaps, close to crowding. Single weight means the trail stands out by brightness alone (it's drawn 0.5 px heavier as the one exception).
